texts.preamble: T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Kabc020092812021 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Additional Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.1314/2021 Dated this 12th day of November, 2024 Petitioner: T. Kishore S/o T. Krishnamoorthy, Aged about 38 years, R/at No.9-116-A, Buggakduva, Madanapalli, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh - 517 325. (Smt. Asha A., Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. United India Ins. Co. Ltd., Regional Office, Motor Third Party Claims, Hub, 5th & 6th Floor, Krishi Bhavan, Hudson Circle, Bengaluru. (Insurer of vehicle No. 2 Mvc No.1314/2021 Ap-03-X-6765, (Policy No. 0516823119P106644740)) T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/ 1 (Sri B. T. Rudra Murthy, Advocate) 2. Mrs. K. Bharathi W/o K. Gangadhar, R/at Door No.3-109, Melumdoddi Village and Post, Punganur,Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh - 517247. (Owner of vehicle No.AP-03-X- 6765) (Ex-parte) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in at road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 04-06-2020 at about 5.20 a.m., near 150th Mile, on Madanapalli-Punganur road, NH-42 H/O Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, when the petitioner was riding a two-wheeler bearing No.AP-03-M-4106, slowly and steadily, following all traffic rules and regulations, along with his younger brother, at that time the driver of the passenger auto-rickshaw bearing No.AP-03-X-6765 came in rash and negligently, without caring for human safety and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital and then Helious Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as mechanic and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Madanapalli Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said auto for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/ 2 Auto-rickshaw bearing No. AP-03-X-6765 and its validity as on the date of accident. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
texts.arguments: It has further contended that, the driver of the offending autorickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate. Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of the respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. It has contended that, as per the police documents, the petitioner was solely responsible for the accident. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 knowing that his driver was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the auto-rickshaw, has entrusted the said vehicle to him. Further, the said auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/ 5 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,74,000 X 15/100 X 15 = Rs.3,91,500/-. T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/ 7 ii) Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc. 23. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, the Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy clearly speaks that, the policy covers the risk provided the driver of insured vehicle holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident and he is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act, even if it is fundamental breach. 25. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager V/s Yallavva and another, reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239, has clearly held that, " i) Having regard to Section 149(1) R/w Section 149(7), whenever a case falls under Section T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/ 10 149(2)(a) and the same is successfully established or proved by the Insurance Company, as per the twin tests laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Swaran Singh, nevertheless, the insurer or Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the award vis--vis a third party and is entitled to recover from the insured. ii) The Insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under Section 149 (2), even if it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident) and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act. ix) The judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Subramanyam, holding that a pay and recovery order cannot be made as there is no liability to pay or satisfy the award or decree in respect of a case falling under Section 149(2) is not correct. Hence, that portion of the judgment in Subramanyam, which states that if the case falls within the scope of Section 149(2) of the Act and the insurer is successful in establishing any of the defence as stated therein, it would be completely absolved of its liability to satisfy the award is also not correct and to that extent, it is held to be bad in law."
